what: A closed chain transfers rotation between sprockets on separate shafts. A chain couples separated shafts in the same direction with a tooth-count ratio.
try: Reset and run the example. Watch a link pass around both sprockets.
Compare input and output turns through the full forward-and-reverse motion.
Predict what a larger driven sprocket does before changing a design.
why: The same chain speed passes both pitch circles. A larger sprocket advances through fewer turns for that chain travel. An uncrossed chain keeps both shafts turning in the same direction.
matters: Chains transmit motion across distances that a direct gear mesh cannot span.
question: Does an uncrossed chain reverse the output like one external gear mesh?
answer: No. Its two sprockets turn the same way. The speed ratio comes from their tooth counts.
further: Compare the long 16:24 chain with the smaller 8:24 example.
Explain why correct chain length and shaft spacing both matter.
formula: ωout / ωin = input sprocket teeth / output sprocket teeth
